nodes.description: Once activated (for example by IL-2 or infection-associated cytokines), NK cells from TAP-deficient patients kill autologous HLA class I-low cells, and cytokine induction of HLA class I does not protect TAP-deficient cells.

evidence.reference_title: Inefficient protection of human TAP-deficient fibroblasts from autologous NK cell-mediated lysis by cytokines inducing HLA class I expression.
evidence.snippet: These results suggest that activated TAP-deficient NK cells are strongly cytotoxic to normal autologous cells and that these cells cannot be efficiently protected by cytokines inducing HLA class I expression.
